steps.tx: Severe symptoms of **hyponatraemia**, seizures or deep coma, are treated with a 100 to 150 mL bolus of **3% saline** over 10 to 20 minutes, which can be repeated twice. The aim of the bolus is a rise of about 4 to 6 mmol/L. Rapid partial correction reduces brain swelling and terminates herniation.

steps.tx: The European limit is a rise of at most 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L in the next 24 hours, with a tighter limit of 8 mmol/L in the first day for high risk patients. Overcorrection risks **osmotic demyelination**. Patients with chronic alcoholism, malnutrition, or advanced cirrhosis are exceptionally vulnerable to pontine myelinolysis.

rows: Strictly limit to 6 to 8 mmol/L in advanced liver disease
Continuous monitoring to prevent rapid overshooting
Irreversible flaccid quadriplegia and pseudobulbar palsy

steps.tx: If sodium rises too fast, **desmopressin** and **5% dextrose** are used to re-lower it. Free water restriction alone will not catch a rapid aquaresis. When the underlying cause of hyponatraemia resolves, sudden spontaneous water excretion can drive sodium concentrations up dangerously, requiring proactive clamp therapy with synthetic vasopressin analogues.

left.title: Aquaresis identification
points: Urine output surges over 200 mL per hour
Urinary osmolality drops below serum osmolality
Serum sodium increases faster than 1 mmol/L per hour

right.title: Rescue re-lowering strategy
points: Administer desmopressin 1 to 2 mcg IV to halt aquaresis
Infuse intravenous 5% dextrose to replace deficit
Re-establish safe trajectory under 8 mmol/L per day

steps.tx: **Hypernatraemia** is a **free water deficit**. The deficit is replaced slowly, usually no faster than 10 mmol/L per day, unless the rise was acute over minutes, as in salt poisoning. Brain cells generate idiogenic intracellular osmoles during chronic hypertonicity, so rapid rehydration causes lethal intracellular cerebral oedema and seizures.

Brain cells generate idiogenic intracellular osmoles during chronic hypertonicity, so rapid rehydration causes lethal intracellular cerebral oedema and seizures.

rows: Replace free water deficit slowly using enteral water or D5W
Osmoles have not accumulated; rapid lowering is safe
Add ongoing insensible and urinary free water losses

steps.tx: ECG changes of **hyperkalaemia** are treated with **intravenous calcium**, which stabilises the membrane and does not lower the potassium. **Insulin with glucose**, and nebulised salbutamol, shift potassium inward. Removal is by diuretic, resin, or dialysis. Calcium chloride restores normal resting myocardial membrane potential within three minutes.
steps.say: ECG changes of hyperkalaemia are treated with intravenous calcium, which stabilises the membrane and does not lower the potassium. Insulin with glucose, and nebulised salbutamol, shift potassium inward. Removal is by diuretic, resin, or dialysis. Calcium chloride restores normal resting myocardial membrane potential within three minutes.

left.title: Membrane stabilisation
points: Calcium chloride 1 g or calcium gluconate 3 g IV
Rapidly reverses peaked T waves and widened QRS
Zero effect on actual serum potassium concentration

right.title: Intracellular shifting
points: Regular insulin activates Na+/K+ ATPase pumps
Sodium bicarbonate useful in metabolic acidosis

steps.tx: A standard shift dose is 10 units of regular insulin with 25 g of glucose. The glucose is checked for hours because **hypoglycaemia** outlasts the potassium fall. Peak potassium lowering occurs at thirty to sixty minutes, but the biological half-life of intravenous insulin frequently induces delayed severe hypoglycaemia up to six hours later.

Peak potassium lowering occurs at thirty to sixty minutes, but the biological half-life of intravenous insulin frequently induces delayed severe hypoglycaemia up to six hours later.

rows: Hourly checks for at least 4 to 6 hours
Detects late hypoglycaemia after insulin clearance

steps.tx: **Refeeding syndrome** drops phosphate, potassium, and magnesium when carbohydrate is restarted. **Thiamine** is given first, calories are increased slowly, and phosphate is replaced before a cardiac arrhythmia. Glucose administration stimulates insulin release, driving extracellular electrolytes into cells for carbohydrate phosphorylation and ATP generation.

left.title: Electrolyte shift consequences
points: Severe hypophosphataemia halts cellular ATP production
Acute thiamine consumption precipitates Wernicke encephalopathy

right.title: Preventive critical care protocol
points: Administer high-dose parenteral thiamine prior to feeding
Start caloric delivery cautiously at 10 kcal/kg/day

steps.tx: **Hypomagnesaemia** causes refractory hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia. Magnesium is replaced before expecting the potassium to stay up. **Deep tendon reflexes** are watched when magnesium is infused. Intracellular magnesium is an essential cofactor for Na+/K+ ATPase and parathyroid hormone secretion, so hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia resist correction until magnesium normalises.
